posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption:
Few places feel as unexpected as Playa del Amor.⁠
⁠
After swimming through a 24-meter tunnel, you emerge onto a secluded beach hidden inside a giant open-air crater.⁠
⁠
Once shaped by military testing, the Marietas Islands are now a protected national park, and only a small number of visitors are allowed to enter each day.⁠
⁠
By: @darkres14 @jorge__medina_⁠

Japan introduced the term “kokushobi” (極暑日), meaning an extremely hot day, to better communicate the dangers of intense summer heat.⁠
⁠
With temperatures and humidity reaching uncomfortable levels, Tokyo has introduced cooling spaces known as “human fridges” to help people take a break from the heat.⁠
How hot is it where you are?⁠
⁠
🎥: @kyanasue

This is not a traditional theater experience.⁠
⁠
In Chongqing, China, the Chongqing 1949 Grand Theatre was built specifically for one large-scale immersive production that brings history to life through a fully rotating stage.⁠
⁠
Visitors are slowly moved through different scenes as massive sets, actors, and effects surround them from every direction.⁠
⁠
By: @chongqing1949_theatre @laurahwclx

A fresh krapfen enjoyed at Rifugio Friedrich August, surrounded by the breathtaking mountain views of the Dolomites, is the kind of simple moment that makes a trip unforgettable.⁠
⁠
Because some experiences just taste better with a view. 🇮🇹🥐⁠
🎥: @antoniodimaiolo_

Located in California, JW Marriott Desert Springs Resort & Spa has one feature that makes it distinct from other hotels. You can take a boat tour through the resort’s private waterways.⁠
⁠
The ride gives guests a different way to experience the property, passing through lagoons and surrounding scenic areas.⁠
⁠
By: @marriottbonvoy @jwmarriott_desertspringsresort

Fingal’s Cave on Scotland’s Isle of Staffa is famous for the way crashing waves echo through its towering basalt columns, creating a sound that feels almost musical.⁠
⁠
Formed millions of years ago by volcanic activity, the cave’s unique shape turns the ocean’s roar into deep, haunting notes that have inspired artists and musicians for centuries.⁠
⁠
When composer Felix Mendelssohn visited, the cave’s atmosphere inspired his famous piece The Hebrides Overture.⁠
⁠
By: @dominikagregus

In the Turkish Riviera, there is a fishing boat where grandmas turn a simple meal into an unforgettable experience. ⁠
⁠
This is a unique tradition, where local grandmothers prepare fresh gözleme, a traditional Turkish flatbread filled with delicious ingredients and cooked by hand.⁠
⁠
A beautiful way to experience Turkish culture through food, family, and the sea. 🌊🥙⁠
🎥: @diana.in.diana

What if dinner was not just a meal, but a journey through different worlds?⁠
At Absurdities in Singapore, guests move through six themed rooms, with each space revealing a new course of a six-course dining experience. ⁠
⁠
Visitors climb, crawl, and explore their way through the restaurant as each dish becomes part of the story.⁠
⁠
The immersive experience combines food, design, and theatre, creating a dinner unlike a traditional restaurant visit.⁠
⁠
By: @absurditiessg @togiehajeap

@fishingwithconner just reeled in an impressive catch. 🎣⁠
Can you guess the name of this fish?

Small enough to fit in your hands, yet built to survive some of the toughest environments on Earth.⁠
⁠
Pikas are tiny relatives of rabbits and hares found across parts of Asia and North America. While some species live among rocky mountain slopes, others make their homes in grasslands and meadows.⁠
⁠
Their round ears, short tails, and compact bodies give them their unmistakable “little furball” look. ⁠
⁠
By: Александр Велигура

Mexican cuisine just reached a historic milestone. 🌮⁠
⁠
Californios in San Francisco became the first Mexican restaurant in the world to earn three Michelin stars, one of the highest honors in fine dining.⁠
⁠
Chef Val Cantú’s restaurant brings together the flavors and traditions of Mexico with California’s ingredients, turning familiar dishes into an inventive tasting menu.⁠
⁠
Would you try a meal here?⁠
⁠
By: @californiossf

This festival in Mongolia pays tribute to the legacy of the Mongol Empire. 🏹⁠
Featuring traditional sports, horseback riding, archery, cultural performances, and historic reenactments, it offers a glimpse into the traditions that shaped one of history's greatest empires.⁠
⁠
🎥: @valeriaaa.cuervo

Called ER-100, and co-developed by molecular biologist David Sinclair, it aims to return damaged optic nerves to a more youthful state. Koalas face numerous challenges, but chlamydia is one of the gravest. In many populations, around 50 percent of the marsupials are infected, leading to issues such as infertility, blindness, and starvation. As the disease spreads through wild populations, Australia has approved a vaccine that could become an important new tool for protecting the vulnerable species.

Find out more about the race to save koalas at the link in bio. 

Photograph by @joelsartore

Photo by @robemburyphoto | Looking up at the Milky Way will never cease to inspire me. We are very lucky to have access to beautiful dark skies here in Australia, even close to major cities. This image is a single 20-second exposure showing the Milky Way’s galactic core rising in the eastern sky, with Melbourne’s light glow visible to the right.

This photo was featured in our @natgeoyourshot #NatGeoYourShotNightSky challenge.
